title: Rest on Me
scene: Early 1970s Los Angeles singer-songwriter pop rock
notes: Early pop-rock songwriting and soulful covers supported by a live Los Angeles session ensemble.

title: Kim Carnes
scene: Mid-1970s Los Angeles country-pop and soft rock
notes: Country-tinged soft rock pairs intimate songwriting with polished piano, organ and string arrangements.

title: Sailin'
scene: 1970s Muscle Shoals country-soul and soft rock
notes: Muscle Shoals rhythms join acoustic country instruments, restrained soul accents and reflective ballads.

title: St. Vincent's Court
scene: Late-1970s Los Angeles pop rock and adult contemporary
notes: Varied Los Angeles arrangements balance country warmth, pop-rock drive, saxophone and rhythmic experiments.

title: Romance Dance
scene: 1980 Los Angeles soft rock and adult contemporary pop
notes: Warm soft rock and soulful covers retain Carnes’s grainy vocals before her electronic breakthrough.

title: Mistaken Identity
scene: 1981 Los Angeles pop-rock and emerging new-wave crossover
notes: Bright analogue synth hooks and dry live-band drums underpin husky pop-rock and intimate ballads.

title: Voyeur
scene: 1982 Los Angeles synth-pop and post-new-wave rock
notes: Pulsing synthesizers and electronic percussion intensify the darker pop-rock approach of her breakthrough.

title: Café Racers
scene: 1983 Los Angeles radio pop-rock with new-wave and AOR production
notes: Polished guitars, driving keyboards and pop ballads balance streamlined new-wave colour with adult contemporary songwriting.

title: Barking at Airplanes
notes: Taut programmed drums and shimmering synths meet sharp guitars and smoky, anxious pop vocals.

title: Light House
scene: 1986 Los Angeles adult-contemporary and electronic pop-rock
notes: Linn-programmed rhythms and glossy keyboards support husky ballads, guitar hooks and layered harmonies.

title: View from the House
scene: Late-1980s Nashville country and roots-rock crossover
notes: Nashville players restore organic country textures; one song retains synthesizers and programmed drums.

title: Checkin' Out the Ghosts
scene: 1991 Los Angeles West Coast soft rock and adult contemporary
notes: Japan-only soft-rock set blends live players, measured programming, expressive vocals and occasional choir.
